from.place: ## Proof, first sentence: the conductor equality in Varieties Remark 09NW used in the extension-by-zero argument

title: The conductor ideal restricts isomorphically to one reduced component
statement: Let $Y$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme] whose underlying space is the union of finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$, each with its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\subset Y$ be the reduced closed subscheme supported on $Z_2\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $i_1:Z_1\hookrightarrow Y$ be the component immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J_1$. Write $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}=i_1^*\mathcal I$ for the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and let $\mathcal I_1\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_1}$ be the image of the induced map $i_1^*\mathcal I\to i_1^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_{Z_1}$. Then the natural map $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}\to\mathcal I_1$ is an isomorphism; equivalently, $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1=\mathcal I\mathcal J_1$, where $\mathcal I\mathcal J_1\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ is the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal J_1\to\mathcal O_Y$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Varieties Remark 09NW (varieties-remark-conductor), applied to the reduced component cover

proof.text: The product $\mathcal J_1\mathcal I$ (the image of $\mathcal J_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal I\to\mathcal I$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], generated by the local products $ab$ with $a$ a section of $\mathcal J_1$ and $b$ of $\mathcal I$) is contained in $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1$, since $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J_1$ are ideals; and $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1=0$ by [lem-sc-conductor-ideal-zero-intersection]. So $\mathcal J_1\mathcal I=0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] the unit $\eta_{\mathcal I}:\mathcal I\to i_{1,*}i_1^*\mathcal I$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal J_1\mathcal I=0$, i.e. an isomorphism. By naturality of the unit [def-pc-module-pullback], $\eta_{\mathcal I}$ followed by $i_{1,*}$ of the map $\varphi:i_1^*\mathcal I\to i_1^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_{Z_1}$ is the inclusion $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ followed by $\eta_{\mathcal O_Y}=i_1^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to i_{1,*}\mathcal O_{Z_1}$, whose kernel is $\mathcal I\cap\ker(i_1^\sharp)=\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1=0$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. As $\eta_{\mathcal I}$ is an isomorphism, $i_{1,*}\varphi$ is injective, i.e. $\varphi$ is injective on $U\cap Z_1$ for every open $U\subseteq Y$; these are all the opens of $Z_1$ since $i_1$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $Z_1$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence $\varphi$ is injective and its corestriction $\mathcal I|_{Z_1}\to\mathcal I_1$ onto its image is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The product $\mathcal I\mathcal J_1$ (the image of $\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal J_1\to\mathcal O_Y$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]) is contained in $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1$, since both are ideals, and $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1=0$ by [lem-sc-conductor-ideal-zero-intersection]. Therefore $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J_1=\mathcal I\mathcal J_1=0$, which is the equality of the statement.
